researcher: Codex parallel northwest research, integrated by Codex

sources.title: National Museums Scotland: Dunadd Hillfort
sources.note: Opening; War, Peace and Craft: sixth-ninth-century Dál Riata, kindreds, food processing, craft and political change. Separate an early Scots label from all later Scottish people.

sources.title: University of Glasgow: Dunadd Digital Archive
sources.note: Excavation synthesis: seventh-century fine metalworking workshop; brooch moulds, tenth-century motif piece, imported pottery/glass, querns.

sources.title: Historic Environment Scotland: Iona Abbey history
sources.note: Columban foundation 563, sea links, early crosses and later thirteenth-century abbey; Book of Kells production qualified as probable.

sources.title: Historic Environment Scotland: Iona monastic settlement, SM 12968
sources.note: Statement of national importance; Adomnán, before 704, mentions fishing nets, deer traps, harvest labour, salt stores, book satchels and ink horns. Earlier contextual evidence, not an 800s household census.

sources.title: Bute Museum: Inchmarnock collection
sources.note: Inscribed slates: Latin/Gaelic, ogham c 7th-9thc, trial letters and designs; distinguish uncertain Hostage Stone interpretation and later thirteenth-century lettering.

sources.title: Cambridge University Press: Western Illuminated Manuscripts, Book of Deer entry
sources.note: Entry 2, Cambridge Ii.6.32: probable Scottish origin, late ninth or early tenth century; 86 parchment leaves measuring 157 by 108 mm; Gospels and prayers for the sick.

sources.title: University of Glasgow DASG: Book of Deer
sources.note: Social Context: Latin main manuscript and twelfth-century Gaelic additions by five hands; do not backdate land-grant notes.

sources.title: University of Delaware: Books, Book Satchels, and Shrines in the Book of Deer
sources.note: Figure 12 and associated discussion identify In principio page, Cambridge Ii.6.32 folio 42r; use only two-word Latin opening.

sources.title: Scottish Archaeological Research Framework: Medieval archaeobotany in Perth
sources.note: Twelfth-thirteenth-century urban deposits: cereals, imported fruits, local berries; waterlogged latrines/middens; moss uses and rural supply.

sources.title: Scottish Archaeological Research Framework: Medieval urban settlement
sources.note: Perth royal burgh, river crossing, burgage plots, organic preservation and skin-working; avoid extending urban sample to every rural home.

sources.title: National Museums Scotland: The story of the Lewis chess pieces
sources.note: Late 12th/early 13thc, likely Norway, walrus ivory and whale teeth, uncertain discovery/burial; Lewis under Norway until 1266. Do not repeat page's oversimplified claim that chess originated in Islamic world.

sources.title: National Records of Scotland: Declaration of Arbroath transcription and translation
sources.note: 1320 letter, paragraph Non enim propter gloriam; archive warns edition reconstructs dispatched letter rather than exact diplomatic reading of SP 13/7.

sources.title: University of St Andrews: History and heritage
sources.note: Teaching 1410, formal university 1413; distinguish an advanced institution from universal schooling.

sources.title: Historic Environment Scotland: St Andrews Castle history
sources.note: Bishops' residence,1546-47 siege and mine/countermine, Reformation 1560.

sources.title: UK Parliament: The Articles, constitution and trade
sources.note: Articles 1, 3, 18 and 19: union on 1 May 1707, a shared parliament, and retained legal institutions.

sources.title: National Museum of Ireland: Ardagh Chalice
sources.note: Eighth-century silver vessel, component manufacture, gold filigree/glass/enamel, apostle names and hoard context.

sources.title: Heritage Ireland: Ardagh Ringfort
sources.note: Discovery in 1868 beneath a flagstone while digging potatoes; the hoard contained a chalice, smaller cup and four brooches.

sources.title: Trinity College Dublin: Book of Kells
sources.note: Production around 800 and uncertain division of work between Iona and Kells; 340 leaves, several scribes and artists, and pigment analysis.

sources.title: James J. O'Donnell, Georgetown University: Pangur Bán
sources.note: Original Old Irish opening and English translations of the poem. The card uses a short literal rendering rather than quoting modern verse translations.

sources.title: National Museum of Ireland: Wood Quay 50
sources.note: Description of research on more than 2,000 combs from Dublin, including a Scandinavian group, their materials, manufacture and wear patterns.

sources.title: National Museum of Ireland: Exhibition galleries guide
sources.note: Viking Ireland gallery: reconstruction of a Dublin house, craftworking and trade. The gallery overview covers finds of different dates.

sources.title: National Museum of Ireland: Clontarf 1014
sources.note: Exhibition reassessing the familiar story of Clontarf as a simple conflict between Christian Irish and pagan Vikings.

sources.title: Cadw: Medieval Wales
sources.note: Regional kingdoms, later princes and subsequent conquests; the atlas interval does not cover the whole history of Welsh communities.

sources.title: Museum Wales: The Palace in the Lake
sources.note: Llan-gors crannog: royal association with Brycheiniog, construction in the 890s, and excavated brushwood, stone and oak palisades.

sources.title: Museum Wales: Llan-gors textile
sources.note: Article dated 3 May 2007: conservation, linen density, silk decoration, hem and belt loop. Both the wearer and the association with the attack of 916 remain uncertain.

sources.title: Museum Wales: Vikings on Anglesey
sources.note: Building phases around 890-970 and 855-1000; leatherworking tools, coins, weights, agriculture and connections across the Irish Sea.

sources.title: Museum Wales: Witnesses to Viking-age North Wales
sources.note: Five burials in a filled ditch, late tenth-century dating and facial reconstruction. The circumstances of death and suggested relationships remain uncertain.

sources.title: RCAHMW Coflein: Conbelin Cross
sources.note: Site 301359: Pennant sandstone, carved decoration and Latin inscription. The name of the person commemorated is incomplete.

sources.title: Cadw: Margam Stones Museum, rainy-day guide
sources.note: The Margam Stones Museum entry dates the Conbelin Cross to the tenth century.

sources.title: UK Parliament: Parliamentary union
sources.note: Legislative union, debates and assent in 1800; implementation 1 January 1801. Do not repeat erroneous 1790 foundation date for United Irishmen.

sources.title: UK Parliament: Meeting Ireland's terms
sources.note: Volunteers 1778, trade restrictions, legislative changes 1782; restricted representative institutions, not modern democratic independence.

sources.title: Marsh's Library: History
sources.note: 1707 Act, public reading, librarian Élie Bouhéreau, collections, reading cages and mid 1760s book losses.

sources.title: Rotunda Hospital: Chronological history
sources.note: Opening history and early fundraising 1746-1757; concerts, plays and lotteries. Exclude modern monetary equivalencies and claims of universal successful care.

sources.title: Irish Linen Centre and Lisburn Museum: Market Square through time
sources.note: Eighteenth-century linen market, brown linen market c 1750, Volunteers 1782; early 1800s assembly room belongs after union.

sources.title: Trinity College Dublin: Jonathan Swift
sources.note: Biography, Gulliver's Travels 1726 and original title; literary satire not factual travel.

sources.title: Royal Dublin Society: Our history
sources.note: Foundation 1731; forestry premiums from 1742, drawing school 1750 and architectural drawing 1760s.

sources.title: National Archives of Ireland:1922 Constitution Committee
sources.note: Constitution adopted by Dáil 25 October 1922; distinguishes Free State constitution from 1937 Constitution.

sources.title: Electronic Irish Statute Book: Constitution, Irish text
sources.note: Article 4: Éire is ainm don Stát nó, sa Sacs-Bhéarla, Ireland. Online text uses standardized modern Irish; do not label it a 1937 facsimile.

sources.title: Electronic Irish Statute Book: Republic of Ireland Act commencement
sources.note: Whole Act in force 18 April 1949, commencement order 1949.

sources.title: ESB Archives: Rural electrification
sources.note: 1946 launch, first pole Kilsallaghan 5 November 1946; scope 792 rural areas.

sources.title: ESB Archives: More Power to the Farmer,1957
sources.note: Primary promotional film: hand washing, carrying water, butter churning; signing up, costs and sceptical customers. Images support promotional representation, not a national census.

sources.title: Central Statistics Office:1961 Census, Volume 6
sources.note: Table 33, page 161: 301,774 farm dwellings; 237,904 using a well, fountain, pump or other water source; 30,943 with a fixed bath and 31,500 with a hot-water tap.

sources.title: Department of Education: Provision of Free Post Primary Education
sources.note: Circular published 1 February 1967; free post-primary policy.

sources.title: Comptroller and Auditor General: Appropriation Accounts 1967-68
sources.note: Education account records free school transport from 1 April 1967.

sources.title: UNESCO: Hurling
sources.note: 2018 living-heritage description: teams, skills, clubs, volunteers and intergenerational transmission. Do not present claimed 2000-year antiquity as a precise archaeological date.

sources.title: European Union: History 1970-79
sources.note: Ireland, Denmark and UK entered European Communities 1 January 1973.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: Middle Ages 1000-1536
sources.note: Christian kingdom, landowners, agriculture, towns and trading; avoid material about Greenland as evidence for Danish households.

sources.title: Kirstine Haase, Museum Odense: Hvad baggårdene gemte
sources.note: Thomas B. Thriges Gade excavations: brick houses, barrel latrines, possible wiping equipment, animals and gardens in medieval Odense.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: Lisbjerg golden frontal
sources.note: Collection photograph and record: Madonna and Child, golden altar frontal from Lisbjerg Church,1135.

sources.title: UNESCO: Roskilde Cathedral
sources.note: Twelfth-thirteenth-century Gothic brick cathedral and regional architectural influence; later chapels/royal mausoleum chronology distinct.

sources.title: Royal Danish Library: Codex Holmiensis, Jyske Lov
sources.note: 1241 issuance at Vordingborg; king, sons, bishops and leading men, application Jutland/Funen; distinguish composition from manuscript copies.

sources.title: Lund University Library: Medieval manuscript 25
sources.note: Lund manuscript 25, dated between the fifteenth and mid-sixteenth centuries; Danish prologue begins on folio 2r. It is a later copy of the 1241 law.

sources.title: Danmarkshistorien: Kalmarunionen 1397-1523
sources.note: Scholarly history, Margrete and Erik, union 1397; separate kingdoms under shared monarch.

sources.title: Danmarkshistorien: Denmark and Estonia c 1200-1645
sources.note: Danish northern Estonian possessions and 1346 sale; later claims do not undo the sale.

sources.title: Þingvellir National Park: Lögberg
sources.note: The Commonwealth and the law speaker’s three-year cycle; procedural rules were repeated annually. The exact medieval Law Rock location remains uncertain.

sources.title: Þingvellir National Park: Centre of social life
sources.note: Assembly gathering and temporary turf/stone/wood/textile booths; visible remains mostly much later than Commonwealth.

sources.title: UNESCO: Þingvellir National Park
sources.note: Althing founded 930, outdoor assembly until 1798, archaeology and cultural landscape; later remains not all 930.

sources.title: David Beard: The excavated farm at Stöng
sources.note: Archaeological educator's description of 1939 excavation: farmhouse plan, pantry/vats, outshoot commonly interpreted as latrine, byre/smithy/church. Abandonment claim 1104 is qualified by separate peer-reviewed source.

sources.title: Dugmore and colleagues: Abandoned farms, volcanic impacts and woodland management
sources.note: Arctic Anthropology 44(1), 2007, pages 1 to 11: nine soil profiles, 92 ash layers and evidence for regional activity continuing after 1104.

sources.title: Árni Magnússon Institute: Grágás
sources.note: Decision to record law in 1117, surviving manuscripts, and the contents and later reuse of mid-thirteenth-century fragment AM 315b fol.

sources.title: Árni Magnússon Institute: AM 677 4to, spiritual food
sources.note: Manuscript AM 677 4to, around 1200: Christian translations, writing conventions and a quotation presented in modernized Icelandic spelling.

sources.title: Alþingi: History and institutions
sources.note: Historical section: Old Covenant 1262-1264 and Norwegian royal allegiance; later assembly continuity.

sources.title: University College Cork: Pangur Bán text and manuscript description
sources.note: Manuscript sources: Unterdrauberg, Carinthia, Codex Sancti Pauli; scholarly edition of original Old Irish poem.

sources.title: University College Cork: Early Irish Lyrics programme
sources.note: Monastic poems, ninth century: Messe ocus Pangur Bán.
